records.quote: I ran test_inference on a 3090 and a Xeon E5 CPU on Windows and the process was most likely CPU bottlenecked; I got ~80t/s with llama2 7b EXL2 4bpw
records.notes: test_inference on 3090 + Xeon E5 CPU, Windows; author reports one Xeon core pinned at 100% @ 3.8 GHz, most likely CPU bottlenecked; ~80 t/s as reported

records.quote: I got ~20t/s with 70b EXL2 2.5bpw, which is about 50% and 70% of the speed listed for a 3090Ti; generation apparently fully loads the GPU @ 98% utilization and 400w tdp; Any chance that the inference performance can still be improved on Xeon CPUs that are clocked lower?
records.notes: test_inference on 3090 + Xeon E5 CPU, Windows; ~20 t/s as reported, GPU at 98% utilization / 400 W tdp per author; source names the model only as '70b', Llama 2 implied by the paired llama2 7b run

records.quote: Here's my batching/caching API I made over the weekend. 200+ tk/s with Mistral 5.0bpw.exl2 on an RTX 3090 with concurrent requests; It was for a personal project, and it's not complete, but it's very fast.
records.notes: title-level claim: 200+ t/s aggregate with concurrent requests through the author's own batching/caching API (EricLLM), a drop-in vLLM replacement; body links the repo without per-request numbers

records.quote: run a quick speed test using the Llama 3 8B Instruct Q8.0 quants in both LM Studio and EXUI; i7-14700K, 64GB DDR4 4300MHz of RAM, RTX 4070Ti Super 16GB VRAM, Windows 11 Pro; List the first 30 elements of the periodic table, stating their atomic masses in brackets.
